newsitem.title: USA: Willis' "Element" remains top movie at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Willis' "Element" remains top movie at U.S. box office.

text.p: The Bruce Willis sci-fi picture "The Fifth Element" was the top film at the U.S. box office for the second consecutive weekend, during which the top five films were unchanged from the prior period, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

The top 10 contained only two new entries, "Night Falls on Manhattan," tied for sixth place, and "Sprung" at eighth. The box office is in a holding pattern awaiting next Friday's opening of "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" from Steven Spielberg and Universal Pictures.

"The Fifth Element," a French-made movie that critics have generally termed baffling, earned an estimated $11.6 million in the Friday-to-Sunday period, a reasonable 32 percent drop from last weekend. Its 10-day total stands at $34.4 million. This weekend, it earned an average of $4,640 from 2,500 screens, the highest average in the top 10.
The film was produced by major French studio Gaumont SA and released in the United States by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp.

Warner Bros.' "Fathers' Day" was second with $6.4 million, followed by Paramount Pictures' "Breakdown" with $6.1 million, New Line Cinema's "Austin Powers -- International Man of Mystery" with $5.6 million and 20th Century Fox's "Volcano" with $3.6 million.

Universal's Jim Carrey comedy "Liar Liar," which was sixth last week, had to share that spot this time with "Night Falls on Manhattan," a Paramount crime drama starring Andy Garcia and Lena Olin. The $3,958 per-screen average for "Night" was the second-highest in the top 10.

"Sprung," an urban comedy starring Tisha Campbell and writer/director Rusty Cundieff, earned $2.5 million over the weekend for a $3,205 average -- the third-highest in the top 10. Since opening on Wednesday, the picture has earned $3.0 million. It is released by Trimark Pictures.
Warner Bros. and New Line are units of Time Warner Inc.. Paramount is a unit of Viacom Inc. 20th Century Fox is a unit of News Corp.. Universal Pictures is a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd..
